HEADER.TITLE: Les deux sœurs et leur mauvaise mère

S.FORM: O susrēg ble mraw sa, m-van tm̄e seg.
S.TRANSL: Here comes a story, here’s how it goes.

S.FORM: O rqa valrēg ma i ntōn wo m̄erm̄er rqa sutwal brēmalwo, tuar otik.
S.TRANSL: Once upon a time, there was a woman with her daughter, as well as another girl, a baby.

S.FORM: Tōlnēr togtog avvan, tuar rāvrēv, vverār ron̄: “Tōlgēn s-sēw a Tō. Tōlgēn s-van sālsēl ngatōlgēn o mās.”
S.TRANSL: They were living together, and one day, the mother said: “Alright, let’s walk down to Tō, let’s go fishing.”

S.FORM: Tōlnēr m-sēw ror a Tō nen̄, o m̄erm̄er rqa vilwo sa tan i tuan o brinti tik sa s-togtog tan i vverār s-van sālsēl.
S.TRANSL: So they all walked down to Tō: the older girl, together with her little baby sister, they both followed their mother and went fishing.

S.FORM: Sālsēl sālsēl avvan, brinti m̄erm̄er sa ni me-mrō, ni so tān̄.
S.TRANSL: So the fishing was going on, when suddenly the little baby felt thirsty, and began to cry.

S.FORM: Tān̄tēn̄ avvan i tuan ron̄ “Vēv, nēk s-ron̄ ma sur i meme sei, ni t-tān̄ ti ni va-mrōs so / wedek ni va-mrōs susus.”
S.TRANSL: As she heard her cry, her older sister called upon their mother: “Mother, listen to our baby! She’s crying, she probably wants to be fed.”

S.FORM: Ron̄ “Bek, tuqa, ngakmur o wgargar sutwal.”
S.TRANSL: “No!” said the mother, “She’ll just have to wait, we’ve got one fish for the two of you.”

S.FORM: Avvan, rār m-togtog avvan, tuan sa ron̄ “Nēk s-row mama, nēk s-la o sus min ni ti nēk qra van kēl āt nēk qra sālsēl kēl.”
S.TRANSL: After a moment, the older sister insisted: “Come on, sit down a little, just breastfeed her: right afterwards you can go back down there and start fishing again.”

S.FORM: “Ar tuqa galāg titi! Ngakmur o wgargar me-rō.”
S.TRANSL: “No, she’ll just have to wait! We have two fish for the two of you.”

S.FORM: O brinti m̄erm̄er sa tān̄ tān̄ tān̄ vavvan, tuan ron̄ / m̄erm̄er rqa vilwo ron̄: “Vēv, row ma sur ni!”
S.TRANSL: But the baby couldn’t stop crying, and crying, and crying. The older sister asked again: “Mother, please, come and see her!”

S.FORM: Ni m-tān̄ avvan, na qtegaran t-wow nok ti.
S.TRANSL: As the baby kept crying, her throat was getting sore.

S.FORM: Ni ron̄ wa “Tuqa! Ngakmur o wgargar me-vāt gēn dek le.” 🌿
S.TRANSL: But the mother kept saying “No, wait! You now have four little fish to eat.” 🌿

S.FORM: O m̄erm̄er rqa sa ni m-tog avvan na llon me-ttās sur tuan sa o nti tik, beb atwal wor ni, o brinti m̄erm̄er sa t-tān̄ t' sa, t-tān̄ ti ni me-tur wēgi o wavan vata le naw.
S.TRANSL: The girl was now feeling sorry for her little baby sister, so she took her piggyback; and while the little baby kept crying, she went down to the shore, to pick a pandanus fruit.

S.FORM: Ni m-beb atwal wor ni, ni ron̄ “Va-wē! Vēv! Varvar nēk sur ak nēk s-la m̄o o sus min i tsik la, nēk s-van tēmē ma, va-wē kmār ka me-to.”
S.TRANSL: With her baby sister on her back, suddenly she raised her voice: “Alright, mother! I called you many times so you’d come and feed by baby sister, but you never came. Alright now, we’re out of this place.”

S.FORM: Rār so to. Rār m-to nen̄, rār m-van dēn lē mta mrēsrēs a Tō, rār so rev o nti sri Tō.
S.TRANSL: And off they went. As they fled, they ran away from the coral reefs, and pulled in the small cliff of Tō.

S.FORM: Rār m-rev o nti sri a Tō, rār so to.
S.TRANSL: They pulled the cliff of Tō in front of them, and ran away.

S.FORM: Rār m-van van van avvan, van sag a Dangon, rār so rev mlē tuar sri a Dangon gor i vverār.
S.TRANSL: They ran and ran and ran, until they reached up at Dan’ghon; there too, they pulled in the cliff of Dan’ghon, to block the road of their mother.

S.FORM: I vverār ka m-nōs a Tō wa ni m-kal vga a Tō, rār a Dangon rār so rev mlē tuar sri.
S.TRANSL: As their mother had managed to climb the Tō cliff and go beyond there, the girls had already pulled in a second cliff at Dan’ghon.

S.FORM: Ni me-vrisa srēg rār, ron̄ “Ar row kēl ma!” – “Bek! Kmār m-varvar sē nēk kak s-la o sus min i tsik, nēk so-mrōs tēmē! Bek, kmār me-van atwal wor.”
S.TRANSL: But she kept chasing them! “Come back!” she yelled. “No!” they replied, “We’ve been begging you to feed my sister, and you never would! So now we’re just running away.”

S.FORM: Ni m-van dēn̄ sag a Dangon, ni m-nōs aē avvan, ni m-kal vasul o sri a Dangon.
S.TRANSL: The mother went all the way up to Dan’ghon, went on and on, and then stepped over the giant gape.

S.FORM: Rār m-van rār so rev o sri a Sri-ōw.
S.TRANSL: The two girls ran further away, and managed to pull in the cliff of Sriow.

S.FORM: Rār m-rev o sri a Sri-ōw, i vverār me-tkar rār avvan dēn̄ a Sri-ōw wo vverār s-nōsnōs mōmōl rār so row kal vga, i vverār m-row kal vga, rār m-van sag rār so rev o sri a Lētn̄in.
S.TRANSL: But even though they had pulled the Sriow cliff, their mother kept chasing them all the way to Sriow: she kept charging behind them, jumping and leaping…

S.FORM: Rār m-rev o sri a Lētn̄in, rār m-van dēn a Lētn̄in, vverār m-dēn̄ sag a Lētn̄in, rār so van dēn Lētn̄in, rār so van.
S.TRANSL: This time they pulled open the cliff at Let’ngin. Their mother kept following them up to Let’ngin, so they kept running!

S.FORM: Van sag nen̄ avvan, rār so rev tuar sri a Turtektō.
S.TRANSL: Kept running till they reached Turtektō, where they pulled open the cliff again.

S.FORM: Rār s-tur aē, rār s-tek vagvagē ror ma a Tō le naw, rār m-tek vagvagē a Tō, rār ron̄ “Va-wē, a Tō van dek dār m-van dēn aē.”
S.TRANSL: The two sisters stood on top, above the Tō cliff near the coast. They cast a last glance down over the sea: “Alright,” they said. “This Tō cliff shall be the place whence you and I will leave [this world].”

S.FORM: Rār m-tek vagvagē a Tō rār so van.
S.TRANSL: So they uttered their final words, and left Tō.

S.FORM: Van sag, vverār m-dēn̄ sag a Turtektō, rār m-van atwal nok sag nen̄, rār m-salvut atwal rār so row sag a Mke Grāt.
S.TRANSL: And as their mother reached Turtektō herself, the two girls were already climbing further up. Suddenly they took a leap together, and landed on top of the Ghraat volcano.

S.FORM: Rār m-row sag a Mke Grāt: o m̄erm̄er sa, i vverār t-rāsrēs ma sur rār ti, m̄erm̄er rqa vilwo sa ron̄ /
S.TRANSL: As they landed on the volcano, they saw their mother come closer again.

S.FORM: M̄erm̄er rqa vilwo m-varvar ror le qarn̄a grāt ron̄: “O Vu! O vu, kak nēk aē nen̄? Na s-aqtē āt tarwi tsik sa? Nēk s-gān!”
S.TRANSL: Suddenly, the older sister turned to the volcano’s crater, and exclaimed: “O Spirit! Are you there, Spirit? Let me throw you my sister’s umbrella leaf, let’s see if you’ll swallow it!”

S.FORM: Ni m-aqtē ror tarwi tsēn, o Vu so / rār m-tek wor sē o leb so kal.
S.TRANSL: So she threw her sister’s umbrella leaf down into the crater, and they saw how the volcano spirit pushed up its mud.

S.FORM: Ron̄ kak: “Vu! Nēk aē nen̄? Na s-aqtē āt i tsik, nēk s-gān ni?”
S.TRANSL: Then she exclaimed “Spirit! Are you there? Now I will throw you my sister, let’s see if you swallow her.”

S.FORM: Ni m-aqtē ror i tuan sa, o Vu so gān.
S.TRANSL: She threw her sister down the crater, and the Spirit swallowed her.

S.FORM: Ni m-tek sē o dar so kal, o Vu m-gān nok ni.
S.TRANSL: She could see blood bubbling up: that was the Spirit devouring her.

S.FORM: Ni ron̄ kak “Vu! kak nēk aē? Na s-salvut mlē āt? nēk s-gān na.”
S.TRANSL: Finally she cried “Spirit! Are you still there? Now I will jump myself, and you’ll swallow me!”

S.FORM: I vven sa m-sal-/ I tuan sa m-salvut ror, o Vu so gān mlē ni. Vverār m-dēn̄ sē ma, rār nok obek.
S.TRANSL: So the older sister jumped, and was also devoured by the Spirit. When their mother reached the top of the hill, it was too late, they were gone.

S.FORM: Vverār m-van ma nen̄, m-tān̄ wor tān̄ wor avvan, ni so ris wor o m̄la.
S.TRANSL: The mother cried on and on and on – till she turned into a scrubfowl.

S.FORM: Ni m-ris sē o bsē va-ttās, ni so ris atwal wor o m̄la.
S.TRANSL: She tried to transform into a palm bush, to no avail: she was only able to turn into a scrubfowl.

S.FORM: Ni so to atal wor ni o m̄la. Vverār, ni o m̄la. 🌿
S.TRANSL: And so she ran away as a scrubfowl. The mother had become a mere scrubfowl. 🌿

S.FORM: Alē, susrig vat ma gēn: nēk m-van le m̄ōs, nēk m-vus o m̄la, nēk so vrisa wālōg mē o qtē bsē s-vagvāt.
S.TRANSL: And here’s what we say traditionally. If you walk to the bush and hunt a scrubfowl, you must hold it and run around a palm bush, four times.

S.FORM: Nen̄ en, nēk s-kuk le nēk s-rēn̄ va-m̄gisgis.
S.TRANSL: If you do that, then when you roast it, it will have tender meat.

S.FORM: La kak nēk mte vrisa wālōg tēmē mi o qtē bsē, nēk s-gān o m̄la nen̄, v-marmar.
S.TRANSL: But if you fail to run around a palm bush while holding it, then its flesh will be too hard to eat.
